independent_numerical_replay.reference: sealed M108-r2 independent raw reconstruction and corrected dual-timeline schedule

boundary_attacks.prior_nonempty_then_empty: dispatch edges 3 then 8; empty release waits prior four-token drain and one dispatch edge
boundary_attacks.three_consecutive_empty: dispatch edges 2, 3, 5; third descriptor observes released-bank reacquire edge
boundary_attacks.pwp_hides_dispatch: second dispatch at 8 is hidden by PWP ending at 11; correction begins at 11
boundary_attacks.empty_dispatches_during_prior_commit: empty dispatch edges 8 and 10 overlap shared-lane commit ending at 11 without decreasing lane time
boundary_attacks.final_empty_commit_gate: lane at 7 waits empty controller release at 8, then flush plus three commit cycles ends at 12

findings.finding: The dual-timeline recurrence is independently correct and retains a targeted frozen-M106 VCS counterexample, but there is no integrated commercial trace combining M106, PWP arbitration, accumulator backpressure, flush, and commit.
findings.required_action: Build a bounded combined RTL/reference miter spanning nonempty, empty, zero-PWP, bank-blocked, and commit-boundary descriptors before claiming actual-controller cycle exactness.

findings.finding: The 147456-byte W64 accumulator still assumes one 96-lane signed24 update per cycle, equivalent to a 2304-bit vector RMW contract. Macro latency/RDW, epoch clear, forwarding, commit collision, and full-lane signed24 equivalence remain unproven.
findings.required_action: Select a realizable banked macro/register-file implementation, replay backpressure and hazards, and run final-state numeric equivalence.

findings.finding: PWP and correction work is serialized on one abstract 256-bit lane, but weight/PWP payload addresses, SRAM banking, read latency, conflicts, and arbitration are absent.
findings.required_action: Freeze the memory map and run ordered address/port/latency replay against digest a011720a....

findings.finding: The bound assumes losslessly precompacted PWP requests and correction descriptors with independent availability; source scan, compaction, queue capacity, and delivery bandwidth are outside the model.
findings.required_action: Retain the precompacted service-island label or add a bounded delivery schedule.

findings.finding: The 2.138770x value covers four heldout H67 bottleneck Conv3x3 operators at an assumed common clock. It has no macro-inclusive timing/power, equal-area normalization, complete-network operator coverage, or end-to-end delivery.
findings.required_action: Do not cite the value as physical, equal-area, full-network, end-to-end, or headline speedup.

findings.finding: The immutable r2 contract and RUN_COMPLETE still contain their original positive scheduled admission. The sidecar revocation is correct and frozen by the r3 manifest, but consumers that open r2 alone can miss it.
findings.suggested_action: Ensure any milestone index, baseline registry, or paper evidence table points r2 readers to the revocation and r3 superseding contract.

findings.finding: Several r3 analyzer diagnostics still say M108R2, including record progress, overwrite refusal, and conservation/error messages. This does not affect arithmetic but weakens provenance clarity.
findings.suggested_action: Rename diagnostics to M108R3 in the next non-frozen revision.

headroom_and_risk.assessment: The corrected abstract schedule is convincingly above 2x, but macro or delivery overhead occurring more often than roughly once per 6.83 accumulator updates can consume the margin.
